utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-74-A, The Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we proceed, I would make sure that appellants, in particular, can follow the proceedings in a language that they understand. Mr. Prlic. THE APPELLANT PRLIC: Yes, I'm able to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojic. THE APPELLANT STOJIC: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Everything is fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Praljak. THE APPELLANT PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can follow the case without any problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petkovic. THE APPELLANT PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I hear and understand everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Coric. THE APPELLANT CORIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, everything is all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I now have appearances for the parties, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARSDEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Katharine Marsden for the Prosecution, along with Senior Appeals Counsel Douglas Stringer, our Case Manager Thomas Laugel, and our intern David Hamer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Before calling appearances for the Defence, I need to note that on the 28th of January counsel for Mr. Pusic requested to attend this Status Conference by videolink. Mr. Pusic has provided consent for the Status Conference to be held in his absence, and has indicated that he does not have any issues to raise at this hearing. Under Rule 65 bis (C) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, I grant this request and allow counsel for Mr. Pusic to participate by videolink. I also note that on the 5th of February, 2016, Mr. Prlic filed a waiver of his right to have his counsel and co-counsel present at this Status Conference. So now let's proceed. Could I have the appearance for Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. The Defence of Mr. Stojic is represented by Senka Nozica, attorney, and Adam Ellis, legal representative. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances for Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. On behalf of General Praljak, Nika Pinter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances for Mr. Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, good afternoon. On behalf of General Petkovic, Defence Attorney, Vesna Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, and on behalf of Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: MR. PLAVEC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Drazen Plavec, co-counsel for Mr. Valentin Coric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And appearances for Mr. Pusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation][Via videolink] Good afternoon, Your Honour, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, attorney from Sarajevo on behalf of Mr. Pusic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ibrisimovic. This Status Conference is called in accordance with Rule 65 bis paragraph (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. This rule requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the last Status Conference has been held for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody. A Status Conference serves two primary purposes. First, it allows the appellants an opportunity to express concerns relating to their appeal or detention conditions and for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical condition of the detained persons. Second, it provides an opportunity to update the appellants with respect to the status of their case as well as inform the general public thereof. I note that the last Status Conference was held on the 23rd of November, 2015, and that today's Status Conference was scheduled by an order signed by me and issued on the 11th of January of this year. Let's proceed now and I would like to inquire into the status of detention conditions and health situation of the appellants. If any of the appellants so wishes, this discussion can take place in closed session or in private session. So let me address myself to the appellants straight away. Would any one of you prefer to have this discussion held in private or in closed session? I see no reaction from anyone, so I take it -- the same applies to you, counsel for Mr. Pusic? Yes, okay. Thank you. So we will proceed in open session. Mr. Prlic, in the context of the conditions of your detention and health situation, would you like to raise any issue? THE APPELLANT PRLIC: Mr. President, I have no issues or complaint to make. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Prlic. Mr. Stojic. THE APPELLANT STOJIC: [Interpretation] No complaints, likewise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojic. Mr. Praljak. THE APPELLANT PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no complaints, but I would have a question later if you would allow me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Mr. Petkovic. THE APPELLANT PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no complaints whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Coric. THE APPELLANT CORIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And counsel for Mr. Pusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation][Via videolink] Thank you, Your Honour. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I will deal now with recent procedural history. I shall now update you on the case. All of the appellants' briefs in this case were filed on the 12th of January, 2015; that's a year ago. And all of the Defence and Prosecution respondent's briefs were filed on the 7th of May of last year. The Defence and Prosecution reply briefs were filed on the 29th of May of last year. I note that there have been no new public filings since the previous Status Conference, with the exception of the Scheduling Order for this Status Conference of today, and there are no public motions pending before the Appeals Chamber. There are some confidential motions pending, but I cannot give any details on those precisely because they are confidential. This brings me to the last part of today's Status Conference, and I will be asking both the Prosecution and the appellants whether they have -- whether they would like to raise any issues. I'd like to start with you, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARSDEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We have no issues to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I'll address the appellants one by one. Mr. Prlic first. THE APPELLANT PRLIC: I have nothing to say more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. Stojic. THE APPELLANT STOJIC: [Interpretation] I have nothing further to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Prlic would you switch off your -- yes. Mr. Praljak. THE APPELLANT PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Agius, I want to ask you about a problem that has been bothering me for quite a long time in these proceedings and that is the relationship between the issue that culpability has to be proven beyond all reasonable doubt and on the other hand in many proceedings, sometimes in the entirety of the judgement or in parts of the judgement, there is outvoting between the Judges, 60 per cent versus 40 per cent proven guilt or 30 per cent doubt. According to me, this is absurd because we cannot claim that culpability is 66 per cent, whereas the remaining Judge has doubts amounting to 33 per cent that guilt has been proven beyond all reasonable doubt. That's why I would like to ask you, as President of this Tribunal and as a Judge, to clarify this for me. I have consulted a -- legal authorities and I have not found anywhere that 66 per cent proven culpability is in conformity with the principle that guilt has to be proven beyond all reasonable doubt. If you could give me an answer to this dilemma, I would be extremely grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Praljak, and I appreciate your concerns; however, you need to understand that I -- my function does not include that of giving advice to the parties. If you want legal advice, you seek it from your counsel, from your legal advisor. I can explain something very fundamental and very easy to understand. Decisions in this Tribunal are reached by a majority, sometimes by unanimity, sometimes by majority. So whenever there is not unanimity and there is a majority, say out of five Judges three constitute a majority and two constitute a minority, you still can't look at it from the perspective that you are presented. We're not talking of percentages or not or anything like that. We're talking of whether in the mind of the majority the charges have been proven beyond reasonable doubt or not. The fact that there may be a minority who do not believe that the charges were proven doesn't offset the rule that decisions are taken by majority. But I am sure that your counsel will be able to advise you in detail on this, but thank you for asking me to clarify this matter. Mr. Petkovic, do yu have -- would you like to raise any issue? THE APPELLANT PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] I have no issues, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Coric. THE APPELLANT CORIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have nothing to ask, nothing to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel for Mr. Pusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation][Via videolink] Thank you, Your Honour. We have nothing to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So since there are no other matters to be raised, I bring this Status Conference to an end. Let me assure you all that now that -- since I became President of this Tribunal and I automatically became Presiding Judge in this appeal, I'm talking all the necessary steps to ensure that the momentum, the preparation of the judgement is increased and kept steady. I'm happy with the progress that we are making, and still we are a little bit early to say or to give more details, but I'm hopeful, based on what I -- what I know and what I see. So we'll get back to you as we have more information. I thank you for your attendance and declare these proceedings adjourned. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
